Good afternoon, sir! Welcome to Mr. Henderson's Fine Tailoring. I'm afraid Mr. Henderson himself is away on business in Philadelphia and won't be returning for at least three weeks.

I'm minding the shop in his absence. How may I be of service to you today?

transcript.text: Ah, good afternoon. I am Abraham Lincoln, and I come with a matter of some concern regarding the suit I recently ordered from Mr. Henderson. It appears there are some issues with the craftsmanship that need to be addressed. The stitching is not as straight as it should be, one sleeve is noticeably shorter than the other, and the fabric seems to be of a lower quality than what was agreed upon. I trust that this was not Mr. Henderson's intention, and I kindly request that these discrepancies be rectified promptly.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*frowns slightly and crosses arms*

Mr. Lincoln, I do recall your order being picked up just last week. I'm terribly sorry to hear of your dissatisfaction, sir, but as I mentioned, Mr. Henderson is away and will not return for some weeks yet.

*pulls out a thick ledger and flips through the pages*

However, I must inform you that all custom orders are final upon pickup. The receipt you signed when you collected the garment states quite clearly that no alterations or refunds are given once the suit leaves the shop. This is our standard policy for all custom work, you understand.

*taps finger on the counter*

I'm sure you can appreciate that we cannot be held responsible once a garment has been worn or handled outside these premises. The tailoring was inspected and approved at the time of pickup, was it not?

transcript.text:

It was only upon closer examination at home that these issues became evident. I assure you, I would not have accepted the garment had I noticed such glaring imperfections during the initial inspection.

I do sympathize with your policy regarding custom orders, but I believe in this case, an exception must be made. The quality of workmanship in this suit does not align with the standards I have come to expect from Mr. Henderson's Fine Tailoring. I trust that as a representative of the establishment, you will see the merit in ensuring customer satisfaction and upholding the reputation of the shop. transcript.text:

Mr. Lincoln, I appreciate your eloquence, sir, and I do understand your position. However, I must be direct with you—I have no authority to override the shop's policies in Mr. Henderson's absence. The policy exists precisely to protect the establishment from claims made after a garment has left our care.

*gestures toward the signed receipt in the ledger*

You are a lawyer, sir, if I'm not mistaken? Then you understand the importance of contracts and signed agreements. When you collected the suit, you signed acknowledgment of our terms. Every customer does the same.

*softens tone slightly but remains resolute*

I truly am sympathetic, Mr. Lincoln, but even if I wished to help you—and I confess, your reputation as an honorable man inclines me toward believing your account—I simply cannot authorize alterations or refunds. Only Mr. Henderson himself has that authority, and he is three weeks away at minimum.

*pauses*

If you wish, I can make a detailed note of your complaint in our records, and Mr. Henderson will review it upon his return. Beyond that, my hands are tied, sir. I hope you can understand my position.
